text:
Sara: FYI seeing a 95th-percentile latency jump (~120ms) for small reqs in us-west after the continuous-batcher tweak rolled at 09:12. P99 also up. Tagging @Dan @Oscar.
perf-bot: deploy: heuristic-v2 rolled to runtime-prod/us-west at 2026-03-17T09:12Z — health checks OK.
Dan: Can you paste a profiler snippet + kernel selection logs? Also did KV cache hit rate change?
Sara: Putting the quick logs here. Pulled from the node that showed the worst spike: 
```
[batcher] timestamp=09:13:02 forming batch sizes=[1,1,1,1] seq_lens=[12,15,9,8] token_budget_target=64
[batcher] chosen_policy=token_budget_priority (min_timeout=3ms)
[kernel] selected_kernel=matmul_generic_f32 (fallback=true)
[kernel] note=fast_kernel_unavailable for shapes [1,1,1,1] -> routed to slow path
[kv-cache] hit_rate=0.12 (baseline ~0.48 before tweak)
````
Sara: also saw more frequent KV miss storms when small requests cluster.
Oscar: That token_budget_target looks low for small micro-batches; heuristic-v2 probably packs by token budget and prematurely flushes. If batcher flushes early with very small batch shapes, our optimized fused kernels for small-shape matmuls don't trigger -> slow path.
Jess: Could also be KV contention: more opens to storage backend when cache hit_rate drops. Did the heuristic change TTL for prefix caching?
Sara: No TTL change in this deploy, but packing behavior changed. Queue snapshots from the same host: 
```
queue_len_p50=1 p90=3 p99=8
enqueue_rate_spike=+42% at 09:12
small_shape_fraction went 18% -> 56%
avg_batch_tokens dropped 220 -> 78
````
Dan: So avg_batch_tokens dropped substantially. That explains kernel miss. Two quick mitigations: 1) bump token_budget_target for small-shape requests (e.g., +2x) 2) add kernel-affinity rule to prefer fast small-shape kernels even if batch token budget is under threshold.
Oscar: Agreed. Also we should check the binning logic — continuous-batcher's shape-hash -> kernel mapping may be flaking on single-token padding. Run a quick grep for `shape_hash` in today's logs.
Sara: I started a canary rollback and a targeted canary with `--kernel-affinity=true --token-budget-multiplier=2` on a subset (node set A). Command used: 
``nix
infra-run canary --cluster runtime-prod/us-west --tag heuristic-v2-canary --env "kernel-affinity=1 token-budget-multiplier=2"
```
perf-bot: metric-alert: runtime-prod/us-west 95p latency still elevated (+85ms) at 09:22; CI canary deployment in progress.
Dan: While canary runs, collect pprof heap/cpu traces for the slow-path kernel and nvprof traces for the GPU kernels around 09:12-09:20. Also grab KV backend latency histograms.
Oscar: Quick check: ensure continuous-batcher isn't collapsing small variable-length requests into artificially formed batches with padding N leading to different kernel selection; run `grep -E "form.*batch.*padding" /var/log/runtime/2026-03-17*.log | tail -n 50`.
Jess: If canary shows improvement, we can either (A) ship a hotfix that increases min token budget for small shapes, or (B) revert heuristic-v2 and iterate. Given customer impact, revert is safe.
Sara: Rolled back heuristic to v1 in us-west at 09:45. 95p latency returned near baseline within 2 minutes. Collecting traces now and will upload to the perf board. Opening an RFC for changing the token_budget_target logic + adding kernel-affinity tests to CI.
Dan: Thanks. Action items: Sara collect pprof/nvprof + KV histograms; Oscar audit binning logic and kernel mapping tests; Jess propose CI test addenda for small-shape kernel coverage. I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up sync.
Sara: Thanks all — I'll post links to traces and the rollback diff here when ready. :thumbsup:
